#115820. Industry News: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy

📅 01 Oct 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1096 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Sciencedaily ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy

📅 01 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1096 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) have created a upcoming optical-neural processor that uses light to help identify deepfake videos rapidly and accurately.
  • The key difference is that part of the detection process takes place through the physical propagation of light.
  • The technology is detailed in the study "Scalable, Energy-Efficient Optical-Neural Architecture for Multiplexed Deepfake Video Detection," published in eLight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) have created a upcoming optical-neural processor that uses light to help identify deepfake videos rapidly and accurately. Unlike conventional systems that typically examine videos one after another using digital hardware, the UCLA technology can analyze 15 or more video streams at the same time.

The key difference is that part of the detection process takes place through the physical propagation of light. This allows many videos to be evaluated simultaneously during a single optical pass rather than requiring each one to move separately through a conventional digital processing pipeline.

The technology is detailed in the study "Scalable, Energy-Efficient Optical-Neural Architecture for Multiplexed Deepfake Video Detection," published in eLight. The researchers designed the optical AI system to serve as a high-throughput, attack-resilient first layer of defense for screening large amounts of manipulated and AI-generated video.

The Growing Challenge of Deepfake Detection.

Rapid improvements in generative AI have made synthetic videos increasingly realistic, increasing the need for detection systems that are both accurate and capable of operating at large scale.

Many advanced deepfake detectors depend on enormous amounts of digital computation. A single analysis can require hundreds of billions of floating-point operations, and videos are often processed sequentially. As more content must be checked, both the processing time and energy requirements can rise proportionally.

Digital detection systems face another problem. Attackers can deliberately alter fake videos in subtle ways designed to confuse a detector and make manipulated footage appear authentic.

Professor Aydogan Ozcan and his UCLA team developed a hybrid digital-optical system intended to address both challenges.

A lightweight digital encoder first collects compact information about each video, including spatial, spectral, and temporal features. That information is transformed into a phase pattern and displayed on a programmable spatial light modulator.

The resulting optical wavefront then travels through a free-space-based, passive optical decoder. At the other end, paired optical detectors directly produce an authenticity score for each video.

In effect, the system replaces a computationally demanding digital decoding network with a physical process that can handle many streams in parallel.

Nearly 98% Accuracy Across 15 Videos at Once.

In experiments using visible light, the processor examined 15 Celeb-DF videos simultaneously during each optical pass.

It has been revealed that it achieved an average detection accuracy of 97.79%, along with a sensitivity of 99.86% and a specificity of 95.72%. Sensitivity measures how successfully the system identifies manipulated videos, making the particularly high sensitivity vital for a screening tool designed to keep fake content from slipping through.

The 99.86% sensitivity translated to an average false-negative rate of ~0.14%. In other words, only a very small fraction of manipulated videos were incorrectly classified as authentic.

The researchers also pushed the system further by increasing its capacity to 18 videos in a single optical pass. Even at that level, average detection accuracy remained at 96.13%.

More Optical Layers Boost Performance.

The team found that the processor could also become more capable by increasing the physical depth of its passive optical decoder without substantially increasing energy use or inference latency.

When researchers added two optimized passive diffractive layers while testing more difficult deepfake manipulations, detection accuracy improved by ~6.8%.

These phase-only diffractive layers can be manufactured as passive, static optical structures/surfaces. They perform additional calculations through the diffraction of light, meaning they do not require additional electrical power while the system is performing an inference.

That approach could allow more sophisticated processing without the same energy costs that typically accompany larger digital neural networks.

Testing the System Against Google VEO-3 Videos.

The researchers did not limit their experiments to conventional face swapping deepfakes. They also challenged the processor with videos produced using Google's VEO-3 model.

Newer generative AI systems can create footage that lacks many of the obvious artifacts associated with earlier deepfake technology, making them a more difficult target for detectors trained primarily on older forms of manipulation.

With only minimal fine-tuning, the optical processor achieved 94.80% accuracy and 97.61% sensitivity on previously unseen VEO-3 videos during experiments.

The results suggest that the approach could potentially adapt as generative AI technology continues to evolve.

A Deepfake Detector Designed to Be Harder to Fool.

The optical system also indicated resistance to black-box adversarial attacks and provides inherent protection against white-box attacks.

Part of that security comes from the way the detector physically performs its calculations. Because some of the inference process takes place through diffraction, notable parameters of the optical model are effectively embedded within the hardware.

Recent findings suggest that those parameters can be difficult for an attacker to measure, reproduce, or reverse engineer. That makes reconstructing the detector and designing carefully tailored adversarial changes that can evade it considerably more difficult.

Industry observers note that the processor also continued working reliably when videos were affected by image noise, blur, JPEG compression, and experimental misalignments. According to the researchers, those results illustrate how optical computation could provide a more secure and dependable foundation for some artificial intelligence systems.

A First Line of Defense Against Deepfakes.

Rather than replacing sophisticated digital detectors entirely, the UCLA processor is designed to work as a highly sensitive first stage of a larger detection system.

Massive volumes of video could initially pass through the parallel optical processor. Content identified as suspicious could then be sent to more computationally demanding digital models for a more detailed final assessment.

It has been revealed that such a system could combine the strengths of both approaches. Optical processing could provide parallel operation, low decoder energy requirements, high sensitivity, resistance to adversarial attacks, and the ability to adapt to newer AI video generators, while conventional digital systems could provide deeper analysis when necessary.

The researchers say this combination could eventually be useful for large-scale content moderation, media authentication, surveillance, and other security-critical AI applications.

The authors of this work are Parnian Ghapandar Kashani and Dr. Shiqi Chen, who contributed equally, and Professor Aydogan Ozcan. The researchers are affiliated with the UCLA Electrical and Computer Engineering Department, the UCLA Bioengineering Department, and the California NanoSystems Institute.

Industry observers note that materials provided by Light Publishing Center, Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics And Physics, CAS. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

Industry observers note that the ideal UI testing tool is the one that discovers what your customers discover first: broken layouts, usability concerns that no longer work, and new accessibility issues in all the browsers your users use before a change goes into the repository. In 2026, most frontend teams don't rely on a single tool to do all of that. The best setups involve two layers: a test runner layer that releases the browser and monitors behavior, and a UI testing and review platform that visually checks the outcome and routes changes to the right stakeholders for sign-off.

It has been revealed that even with the right stack, it still relies on what your team needs to catch. Different teams will focus on different points: a QA team trying to automate checkout flows, a design system team defending shared components, and a single developer working on a tight budget will all be somewhere different. This guide is categorized by the job these UI testing tools do, then connects them.

It has been revealed that most "best UI testing tool" lists rank test runners and visual testing platforms against each other as if they were interchangeable. They aren't. UI testing covers four distinct jobs:.

Functional testing: Does the UI respond correctly when a user clicks, types, or hovers?

Visual testing: Does the UI still look right across layout, color, typography, and spacing?

Accessibility testing: Can people using keyboards and screen readers use it, and did this change introduce newly introduced violations?

Cross-browser and device coverage: Does it work in Safari on mobile, not just Chrome on a developer's laptop?

There are also other levels of UI tests. Unit tests test the logic but don't interact with the UI. End-to-end (E2E) tests represent the full user journey in a browser but are difficult to set up, hard to troubleshoot when the bug is a visual detail, and can't practically test every state. Between the extremes of unit tests and E2E tests, component tests simulate each component's behavior in a real browser using fixed inputs, offering speed closer to unit tests and user-level coverage closer to E2E. Many teams maintain a thin layer of E2E tests for critical journeys, and they have component tests for the dozens of states a component may be in.

These tools are organized by job so you can stack them rather than choose one winner.

These platforms sit on top of your test runner. They capture rendered UI, compare it to approved baselines, and give your team a place to review what changed.

Industry observers note that chromatic is a UI testing and review platform made by the Storybook team. It catches visual, interaction, and accessibility bugs in components and pages before they merge, and it gives developers, designers, and product managers one place to review UI changes and sign off. Chromatic's team is the core maintainer of Storybook, which has about 90,000 GitHub stars and 17 million weekly npm downloads, and a Vitest core maintainer on the team built Chromatic's Vitest integration. Chromatic is used by 45 Fortune 100 companies, including GitHub, Shopify, Microsoft, Adobe, the BBC, and monday.com.

Industry observers note that pricing: Free initiative with 5,000 snapshots per month (Chrome only), unlimited projects and users. Starter is $179/month for 35,000 snapshots and adds Safari, Firefox, and Edge. Pro is $399/month for 85,000 snapshots. Enterprise is custom, with SSO, SCIM, SLA support, and data retention. TurboSnap snapshots count as 0.2 of a regular snapshot.

Sources indicate that trade-offs: Chromatic is strongest when your UI is built from components. Teams with no component tests can start from Playwright or Cypress E2E tests, but they'll get the most value once components are covered too. Snapshot usage also grows with each browser and viewport you add, so strategy coverage before you scale it.

Best for: Design system teams, product teams that want designers and PMs to approve UI changes, React Native teams, and Vitest-first teams that want visual testing without baselines stored in the repo.

In a recent development, percy is BrowserStack's visual testing platform. It captures screenshots from your existing tests, renders them across browsers and responsive widths, and highlights pixel differences for review.

Industry observers note that strengths: Framework-agnostic SDKs for Playwright, Cypress, Selenium, and Storybook. App Percy covers native mobile apps. The free plan includes 5,000 screenshots per month with unlimited people and projects.

Sources indicate that trade-offs: Percy is page-oriented, and each page rendered in each browser at each width counts as a separate screenshot, so usage climbs promptly with cross-browser coverage. Percy compares feature branches against a base branch, which teams with complex branching should test early. Reviewers see rendered screenshots rather than an inspectable copy of the code under test, so debugging a diff usually means reproducing it locally.

Pricing: Free tier, then paid looks with fixed screenshot allowances and overage.

Best for: Teams already paying for BrowserStack that want visual checks on page-level E2E tests.

Sources indicate that applitools Eyes uses Visual AI to compare screenshots the way a person would, with match levels that can ignore content changes and focus on layout. Its Ultrafast Grid re-renders captured page states across many browser, viewport, and device combinations.

Strengths: Mature AI matching, broad browser and device coverage, Figma and Storybook testing, accessibility testing, and an MCP server. Higher tiers add AI-driven functional testing and plain-English test authoring.

It has been revealed that trade-offs: Applitools is priced and packaged for enterprises. There's a free trial but no free plan, and the Starter plan is $667/month billed annually for 100,000 component checkpoints or 1,000 page checkpoints. Professional and Enterprise are custom-priced.

Best for: Large QA organizations with major cross-browser matrices and budget for a dedicated visual AI platform.

It has been revealed that backstopJS is a free, open-source visual regression testing tool released under the MIT license. You list the URLs, viewports, and CSS selectors to capture in a config file, and BackstopJS renders them in a headless browser through Playwright or Puppeteer, then compares the results against approved reference screenshots. The core workflow runs on three commands: backstop init, backstop test, and backstop approve.

Industry observers note that strengths: Completely free, with no screenshot limits. A built-in browser report shows reference and test images side by side with a visual diff inspector, and changes can be approved from there. Optional Docker rendering keeps screenshots consistent between laptops and CI; Playwright adds Firefox and WebKit, and click, hover, and keypress selectors capture interactive states. JUnit reports plug into existing CI pipelines.

Trade-offs: BackstopJS is self-hosted, so there's no cloud dashboard, shared team review, or pull request status checks out of the box. Reference screenshots are usually committed to your repository, and every page or component state you want to test needs its own URL and scenario in the config. Someone on the team also has to own the setup, CI integration, and maintenance.

Best for: Developers and small teams with no budget who are comfortable running and maintaining their own visual regression setup.

Industry observers note that test runners click, type, and assert. They're free and open source, and every platform above builds on them. On their own, they offer limited visual testing: built-in screenshot assertions store baselines in your repository, rendering can drift between laptops and CI, and designers have no review interface.

Recent findings suggest that playwright is Microsoft's open-source browser automation framework. It runs tests across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, with auto-waiting, trace viewer debugging and code generation, and supports JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Java, and .NET.

Visual testing: Playwright's toHaveScreenshot assertion compares screenshots against baselines stored in Git. It works, but baselines must be regenerated per operating system, and accepting a change means rerunning with an update flag.

In a recent development, best for: Teams automating critical user journeys such as sign-up, checkout and login. Pair it with a platform like Chromatic for visual review across real browsers.

Industry observers note that cypress is an open-source testing tool that runs inside the browser, with time-travel debugging that indicates the app at each step of a test. It supports both E2E and component testing.

Visual testing: Cypress has no built-in visual comparison and relies on plugins or a platform such as Chromatic, Percy or Applitools. Cypress Cloud, its paid service, adds recording, parallelization, flake detection and add-ons for accessibility and UI coverage.

Best for: Frontend developers who want fast feedback and an interactive test runner while they build.

Storybook is the open source workshop for building UI components in isolation. Each story captures one component state, and those stories double as test cases.

Testing features: Interaction tests with play functions and Testing Library, accessibility checks with the a11y addon, and a Vitest integration that runs stories as component tests.

Visual testing: Storybook doesn't diff screenshots on its own. Chromatic, built by the same team, is its visual testing and review layer.

Best for: Design system and component library teams, and any team practicing component-driven development.

Vitest Browser Mode runs component tests in a real browser instead of a simulated DOM, using Playwright or WebdriverIO under the hood.

It has been revealed that visual testing: Vitest's toMatchScreenshot assertion stores screenshots in the repository. For large projects, this can bloat the repo and baselines drift between machines. Chromatic can take Vitest Browser Mode tests with no code changes and run them in a stable cloud environment instead.

Best for: Teams already writing Vitest tests who want them to check how the UI looks without adopting a upcoming framework.

Start from the problem your team is trying to fix:.

"Shared component changes keep breaking other teams' screens." Test at the component level with Storybook or Vitest Browser Mode and Chromatic, so the change reveals up on the pull request that caused it.

According to recent reports, "Our Playwright tests pass, but the layout still breaks in Safari." Functional assertions don't check appearance. Add a visual testing platform that renders in Safari, such as Chromatic, Percy or Applitools.

"We turned off screenshot tests because of false alarms." Look for deterministic component states and flake controls such as Chromatic's SteadySnap, or AI matching such as Applitools.

"Designers find UI bugs after release." Choose a platform with a review and approval workflow, and make sign-off a required pull request check.

"AI coding agents keep inventing components." Give agents access to your real component library, for example through Chromatic's hosted MCP, and run every agent-built change through the same UI tests as human code.

"We have no budget." Use Playwright or Vitest screenshot assertions, self-host BackstopJS, or start on the free tiers of Chromatic or Percy.

A practical, well-covered setup for a React web app looks like this:.

Unit tests in Vitest for logic and utilities.

Storybook stories or Vitest Browser Mode tests for every meaningful component state, with interaction tests on key components.

Chromatic running visual, interaction and accessibility tests on those components in Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge on every pull request, with designers assigned as reviewers.

A thin layer of Playwright E2E tests for sign-up, checkout and other critical journeys, also captured in Chromatic so page-level visual changes go through the same review.

This keeps most UI coverage in fast, deterministic component tests, while E2E tests confirm the journeys that matter most still work end to end.

Playwright is the best free tool for E2E UI testing, and Storybook is the best free tool for testing component states. For visual testing, For visual testing, Chromatic and Percy both offer free tiers of around 5,000 snapshots or screenshots per month, and BackstopJS is free to self-host.

UI testing is the broad practice of checking that an interface works for users, including functional, visual and accessibility checks. Visual testing is one part of it: comparing rendered UI against approved baselines to catch unintended changes in layout, color, typography and spacing.

According to recent reports, no. Chromatic was built by the Storybook team, but it also runs visual tests from Vitest Browser Mode, Playwright and Cypress tests, and from React Native Storybook on iOS and Android simulators.

Playwright's toHaveScreenshot covers basic visual checks, but baselines live in your repo, rendering can differ between machines, and there's no review interface for designers. Teams with several reviewers or many browsers usually add a platform on top.

Most teams use both. Component tests cover individual UI states rapidly and reliably, while a smaller set of E2E tests confirms that critical user journeys work across the whole app.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 players who used the New Zealand trick to play early on PS5 may have inadvertently purchased a censored version of the game that’s missing a useful stamina buff.

With GTA 6 launching at midnight local time on November 19, impatient fans around the world used the Upcoming Zealand trick to get a head start on their adventures in Leonida.

While Xbox players could simply change their console’s location, PS5 owners had to create a New Zealand PlayStation account and purchase GTA 6 through the country’s digital storefront.

Unfortunately, getting into Vice City a few hours early appears to have come with an unexpected drawback.

As reported by IGN, Rockstar left out the ability to consume cocaine from your inventory in the Australian version of GTA 6, with Latest Zealand reportedly receiving the same version.

Industry observers note that in the international release, players can collect baggies of cocaine or skim some off larger bricks. Consuming cocaine through the item wheel gives players a supercharged stamina bar for roughly 30 seconds.

Australia’s video game classification rules allow depictions of illicit drug use but prohibit players from receiving gameplay benefits for taking them, even in games rated R18+.

Interestingly, Upcoming Zealand doesn’t have this same restriction, but testing by GTA BOOM found that the mechanic was also absent from its New Zealand playthroughs.

Players had already suspected GTA 6 was censored in certain regions before launch when dataminers discovered a roughly 700KB discrepancy in the Australian and New Zealand game files.

Unlike Xbox consumers who temporarily changed their console’s location, PS5 players who bought the Newly introduced Zealand edition still own that regional copy even when playing on their regular account.

Industry observers note that luckily, those affected aren’t missing out on too much. Adrenaline can still be used to boost stamina and other stats, while scripted sequences involving cocaine remain intact.

Still, it’s a rather amusing twist that some of GTA 6‘s most impatient fans ended up with less content than those who waited a few extra hours.

  • It has been revealed that quantum computers rely on qubits to store and process information in ways that conventional computers cannot.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Researchers at the University of Surrey have proposed a newly introduced kind of qubit that could help address one of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing: keeping error rates low as systems become larger.

The concept uses superfluid helium, a form of helium with unusual quantum properties, to create a qubit that may be less sensitive to some of the disturbances that affect today's leading quantum computers.

Why Quantum Computers Struggle With Errors.

It has been revealed that quantum computers rely on qubits to store and process information in ways that conventional computers cannot. Many current systems use superconducting circuits, but these are highly sensitive to electromagnetic noise and stray electrical charges - similar to the static electricity that can make hair cling to a balloon.

It has been revealed that even very small disturbances can disrupt the fragile quantum information stored in a qubit. As more qubits are added, controlling those errors becomes increasingly difficult, making scalability one of the central challenges in quantum computing.

In a study published in npj Quantum Information, researchers from Surrey's Quantum Sciences Group describe a different approach built around superfluid helium-3 - an unusual form of liquid helium that can flow without friction.

According to recent reports, their proposed device, called the Superfluid Helium Oscillator Quantum (SHOQ) device, would use charge-neutral superfluid helium. Because the helium carries no electric charge, the design could be naturally protected from certain types of electromagnetic noise.

A Qubit With Much Lower Predicted Error Rates.

According to the researchers, this is the first reported design for a qubit based on a superfluid. Their calculations suggest the SHOQ device could have error rates about 100 times lower than conventional superconducting qubits.

Dr. Priya Sharma, Daphne Jackson Fellow in Hybrid Quantum Systems at the University of Surrey's School of Mathematics and Physics, and lead author of the study, mentioned:.

"We are not the first to think about the individual components behind this idea, but what we have done for the first time is bring them together in a microfluidic device and work out the specific details that could enable the device to function as a qubit.

Sources indicate that "The maths tells us that it should work. We have taken what we already know about superfluid helium and quantum technologies and turned that into an educated design, with the parameters and specifications needed to build one. The next step is to make a prototype and put those predictions to the test.".

Rather than replacing existing quantum computing hardware, the researchers say the SHOQ device could potentially be integrated with superconducting quantum technology.

That could allow different types of qubits to perform different jobs within the same system, depending on their strengths.

A Possible Role as Quantum Memory.

One longer-term possibility is to use the SHOQ device as a form of quantum memory. In that setup, a superfluid based qubit could store quantum information while other hardware carries out calculations.

According to recent reports, dr. Eran Ginossar, Associate Professor at the University of Surrey's Department of Physics and Advanced Technology Institute, and co-author of the study, said:.

In a recent development, "We don't necessarily need one type of qubit to do everything. Combining different quantum technologies could allow us to take advantage of the strengths of each.

"Superfluid helium gives us a fundamentally different type of quantum hardware to explore. If the predicted performance can be demonstrated experimentally, it could eventually work alongside existing superconducting technologies as part of a larger quantum system.".

The Next Step Is Building a Prototype.

Industry observers note that the team now looks to build a prototype to find out whether the predicted performance can be reproduced in a real device. That effort is being supported by an IAA Commercialisation Fellowship awarded to Dr. Priya Sharma.

The SHOQ device would need to operate at extremely low temperatures, but researchers have already reached the necessary conditions in previous experiments involving superfluid helium-3.

In a recent development, the project was led by the University of Surrey in collaboration with Professor Jens Koch at Northwestern University in the United States. Koch was one of the researchers involved in developing the transmon - a superconducting qubit design that is now widely used in quantum computing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google’s Fitbit Air is one of my favorite products of 2026 and my preferred workout companion, but not being able to see a workout while you’re in the middle of it has been a huge complaint of mine, and the latest Google Health enhancement is fixing that.

Quite literally at the start of this week, I was on a walk through my neighborhood and though to myself, “it’s still pretty annoying that I can’t see my workout progress in the Google Health app.” It’s been a complaint of mine for a while, as various treadmill sessions and more have left me wondering what my heart rate is looking like, how many steps I’ve taken, etc, and it’s only a problem when using the Fitbit Air, seeing as the Pixel Watch (or Fitbit Edge) I’d wear otherwise will show that data front and center.

Google Health 5.13 is fixing that.

In the changelog for Google Health 5.13, Google details a new “exercise in-progress” card on the main “Today” screen. This will show what exercise is being tracked and also let you end the workout early.

Industry observers note that if you use your Pixel Watch, Fitbit Air, or Fitbit Edge to automatically track your exercises, you’ll now see an exercise-in-progress card on your mobile app’s Today screen. This card lets you know that your device is tracking your exercise and gives you the opportunity to end the tracking and get your summary whenever you want.

We don’t know exactly what this card looks like just yet, but it sounds like it fits the need perfectly.

Google Health 5.13 is now rolling out on Android and iOS.

#115813. Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day - all the news and rection as GTA 6 arrived around the world

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3438 w)

Grand Theft Auto 6 launch day - all the news and rection as GTA 6 arrived around the world

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3438 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide.
  • Industry observers note that have you played it yet?
  • Sources indicate that more broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the day is finally here: Grand Theft Auto 6 is available to play worldwide. It's destined to become the largest video game release of all time, and probably one of the biggest entertainment releases of all time. So we're doing a launch day live blog to chart its arrival in the world.

Industry observers note that have you played it yet? I'm curious how many people stayed up until midnight in their region to give the game a go. I couldn't manage it but my college-age son was contemplating it. And if you have played it, what do you think - what are your early impressions? Is this what you were waiting for?

Sources indicate that more broadly, I wonder about the impact GTA 6 will have on the wider world. I've already seen nearly all mainstream news and media outlets attempt to cover the game - and many other kinds of businesses - so will GTA 6 make people reappraise video games?

Moreover, exactly how significant will the launch be? The record books are ready to be written in, but what exactly will be written? And how will other games fare in GTA's wake - better, or worse? There's lots to consider as the ripples spread around the world.

Recent findings suggest that we'll pull-in stories and developments, and your comments, as we chart the arrival of Rockstar's game around the world. Let's get to it.

Our live coverage of this event has finished.

According to recent reports, an historic day in gaming and there's loads to unpack. But to begin with, this: did you take a day off to play GTA 6, and have you played it yet?

Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

According to recent reports, the marketing push by Rockstar to have GTA 6 imprint on real-world cities has been impressive to see. There have been festivals in Miami, Selfridges dedicated a portion of its department store to selling GTA merch, but there's more than this besides. The London Standard summarised much of the activity in London in a video on Instagram.

A post shared by The Standard (@thelondonstandard).

Rockstar employment tribunal verdict could take weeks.

The din of release is in danger of drowning out the Rockstar employment tribunal that came to a close this week in Scotland. Former Eurogamer video producer Chris Bratt - now co-owner of People Make Games - has been following the case closely, and reported yesterday that a verdict in the case could take "weeks".

In a recent development, he quotes Judge Lucy Wiseman as saying: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as quickly as I possibly can.".

And that's it for the Rockstar tribunal! We await the judge's decision, but how long will it take? Judge Lucy Wiseman: "I cannot give a time frame for producing the judgement in this case. What I will say is that I will use my best endeavors to get that judgement out as rapidly as I possibly can.".

Yesterday, we independently confirmed that most, if not all, of the fired Rockstar employees are credited in the GTA 6 credits - which are, according to Chris Tapsell, our reviewer, an enormous thing in their own right.

Here’s how big it is, news-wise:.

Yesterday, my mother _(whose single dabble in gaming over the years can be described as,“working out the way to bypass the Brontosaurus Guarding Causeway in the text adventure Time Machine, is to GIVE it the Ship’s Biscuit found aboard the Marie Celeste”)_ texted me to ask if I was “ready for tomorrow?”.

I instantly assumed I’d made or hinted at some blueprint to do something with her and subsequently forgotten.

Sources indicate that BUT, NO. She was asking if I was ready for GTA. A product I have never mentioned in her presence in all my many years.

So if you’ve got the over-seventies non-gamers talking… I’d say you’ve cracked it.

Goodness! And will your mother also be playing it?

My inbox is flooded with all kinds of brands trying to get in on the GTA 6 hype.

The most recent one? Petrol prices. "Having to refuel your car in GTA 6 adds another layer of realism to the game, but it's something real-life drivers have to think about every time they get behind the wheel," said Beth Fountain, fuel expert at somewhere called Interfuels.

"With petrol and diesel prices remaining high, filling up can take a significant chunk out of someone's monthly budget, particularly for those who rely on their vehicles for work or regular travel.

"While players might find the new mechanic frustrating, it's a reminder of how much we depend on fuel in everyday life and how quickly those costs can add up.".

There's another one from Just Eat, the food delivery company, which has apparently made a real controller with Just Eat order button on it for you to order food while gaming. It's not specifically GTA 6-linked but it's jumping on that bandwagon. The controller is apparently synced to your Just Eat account. Imagine mashing that by accident and having an accidental feast turn up.

"When you're deep into a high-stakes gaming session nothing kills the moment faster than having to pause the action just to sort out food. With the Just ChEAT Button, Just Eat has unlocked the ultimate hack to evade the kitchen, enabling gamers to stay just where they are and locked into play," said Just East UK and Ireland marketing director Tina Koehler.

According to recent reports, it's not clear where you can buy this controller or how much it costs. It's described as "limited edition". I wonder if that means only one has been made.

The goofy things people are already doing in GTA 6.

Many people are playing GTA 6 already of course and doing expectedly bizarre things in it. From lobbing hammers like Crocodile Dundee lobs cans of tinned food, to dropkicking people, to attempting to dive through a car window while oiled up and in one's pants - Connor has rounded up some of the goofiest clips around.

You are brilliant, Eurogamer readers!

I just want to resurface the winning entry to the GTA memories competition we ran at the tail-end of last week, because it's funny and uplifting, and I still smile about it.

My favourite GTA memory is introducing my nan to Vice City.

She'd never played a video game before, so I told her she could pretty much do whatever she wanted.

She spent the first 20 minutes driving around obeying traffic lights and apologising whenever she bumped into another car.

Then she accidentally punched someone.

I don't know what happened, but something just clicked.

Within half an hour she'd stolen a police car, run over several pedestrians and was shouting at the telly because the police wouldn’t leave her alone.

My grandad came in to see what all the noise was about.

Industry observers note that without even looking up she just said, "I'm wanted for murder, Barry. Put the kettle on.".

Genuinely one of the funniest afternoons of my childhood.

Recent findings suggest that I'm on the management team for a charity and they've scheduled their AGM for tonight at 6pm. Of all the dates! I've had to weigh up not doing my duty for selfish video game reasons.

Industry observers note that I must be growing up because I've decided that going to the AGM is the right thing to do and that GTA 6 probably isn't that good, anyway. Right?

Well! Allow the Eurogamer comments to decide. I think you should set GTA 6 up in another room in the building you're holding the AGM in, and find excuses during it to nip out and play. It'll be like a Mrs Doubtfire moment. Nothing can go wrong.

Another email from a shopping comparison site, Idealo, and this time about PS5 Pro demand, which has apparently leapt by 57 percent week on week because of GTA 6. This, by the way, is exactly what the industry was hoping would happen - that GTA 6 would reinvigorate console sales, which were slumping, not least because of their unprecedented rising prices. Apparently the price of PS5 consoles is rising in step with this demand.

"Grand Theft Auto launches are major cultural moments, and GTA 6 is already having a noticeable impact on the wider gaming market, particularly when it comes to console demand," Katy Phillips from Idealo said.

In a recent development, "We're seeing a significant increase in interest in the PS5 Pro, with demand jumping by 57 percent in the week leading up to launch. At the same time, the price of the console has climbed by more than £450 since the end of October.".

GTA 6 videos you might find helpful.

IGN has produced a bunch of good Grand Theft Auto 6 videos I'm surfacing here in case you've missed them. There are a few performance-related videos of the game running on PlayStation and Xbox hardware:.

There's also footage of the first 15 minutes of the first mission:.

And some scuba diving and treasure hunting:.

GTA 6 is Metacritic's highest rated game ever.

A notable moment yesterday was GTA 6 being crowned as the highest-rated game ever on review-averaging site Metacritic. The game at the moment holds a 99 score there, averaged from 156 critics' reviews. The previous champion was the original Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, from 1998, with the same 99 average critics score. Will it retain the title as the days and weeks unfold?

Recent findings suggest that chris' expansive GTA 6 review is of course one of those contributing to that score. "A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

More ridiculous GTA 6 launch piggybacking and this time it's an email with a therapist talking about how the game might help teens with their dating outlooks.

Says Natalie Buchwald, therapist and founder of Manhattan Mental Health Counseling:.

In a recent development, "Psychologists sometimes talk about 'relationship scripts': the unspoken expectations we absorb about how relationships work, what partners owe each other and what success looks like. We pick these up long before we have much experience of our own, from family, friends, online spaces and the stories we see in entertainment.

According to recent reports, "No single film, game or influencer shapes someone's values on its own. What matters more is the overall mix of messages a person encounters, and whether they have the space to question them. That's particularly relevant now that dating advice is so widely available online, where some content frames relationships around status, control or getting something in return, rather than mutual respect.

"That's why the most useful thing parents can do isn't to hand over a set of rules. It's to help young people think critically about the scripts they're picking up. Being curious rather than critical, and asking what they've seen, what they think of it and what they believe makes a good partner, tends to keep conversations open.

"Entertainment can play a helpful role here. A story built around a partnership, like Jason and Lucia's, can give parents a natural, low pressure starting point for conversations that might otherwise feel awkward.".

Industry observers note that chris referenced some of this in his review, praising Jason's tender and caring side, and his not being a toxic asshole. GTA 6 is also the first game to not only feature a couple but a female playable lead, having very much revolved around male fantasies in the past.

You can't use cheat in GTA 6 until you finish the main story.

A reminder that cheats aren't usable in Grand Theft Auto 6 until you've finished the main story. Chris confirmed this yesterday, and offered details about cheats do work in the game when you've unlocked them.

More brand opportunism, this time optician Specsavers, and at least this one has a novel approach: a spoof partnership with a GTA firm that has nothing to do with Grand Theft Auto.

Specsavers is circulating a very budget-looking partnership with a trucking company called GTA Transport. It's billed as a "mix-up" in an email, but it's all far too staged and knowing to really be one.

Industry observers note that "It might not be the GTA partnership I originally had in mind but a deal's a deal," stated Specsavers marketing person Neil Liddle. "I'm pleased to offer every driver at GTA Transport a free eye test.".

Recent findings suggest that bugz Singh at GTA Transport mentioned: "We were surprised when Specsavers got in touch, but we're delighted to be the GTA they've teamed up with. Our drivers spend all day on the road, so they're looking forward to their eye tests.".

The visuals are just something else. Even at this early stage, the story has already got me interested and invested in Jason and Lucia. And to top it all off, when I first started messing around with the car radio, ‘Master of Puppets’ was playing.

The second thing is that like all gtas is serves a reminder of what a hellscape urban America is. I’ve never been to the keys, but what looks like it should be a lovely set of islands is of course mostly a massive highway.

In a recent development, ...long story short, what was intended to be a 1 hour go on a school night ended up being 3 hours and I slept through my alarm and am working from home today! I'll be playing this and pretty much only this for the next month or 2, no doubt...haven't been gripped by a game since Clair Obscure...nice to have that feeling back!

In a recent development, some nice accounts of playing the game so far. Keep 'em coming!

GTA 6 developers fear for their jobs now the game has shipped.

Rockstar and Take-Two stand to make billions of dollars from GTA 6, but there's an enormous workforce - 4,711 people at last count - working at the GTA studio. Will they keep their jobs now the game has come out? That staff-count more than doubled after Red Dead Redemption 2 was released but will it grow again now?

In a recent development, fears of lay-offs reach top volume both as the game is released and as Rockstar workers vote wheter to formally recognise a workers union there - a union that's proved so problematic in the past. Sherif has the full story below.

GameStop boss slams 'code in a box' trend in wake of GTA 6's discless release.

The boss of game-related retailer GameStop has spoken out about the trend of 'code in a box' game releases. This, of course, is pertinent this week with the discless release of GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that "When you buy a game, you should be able to sell it, trade it or lend it to a friend," GameStop boss Ryan Cohen told Bloomberg. "Unquestionably, the decision to move to all digital has hurt consumers, and it's also hurt GameStop." Dom has the full story:.

Recent findings suggest that I have always wondered if one of the reasons I bounced off 5 was that I got it a long while down the line. (Also... I really didn't like the main characters).

Decided to be part of this "global media event" and bought it last night.

The intro is pretty gripping story wise, with a decent twist that somehow was kept completely under wraps.

Driving takes some getting used to, but the use of adaptive triggers on PS5 is great for this making cruising fairly easy. The traffic density and “smaller” roads really make getting about the city nicely realistically annoying. Spending more time cruising than normal for a GTA.

Being quoted is the risk one runs!

The spoof websites aren't in GTA 6 because Rockstar didn't think they were "necessary".

According to recent reports, the spoof websites of previous GTA games don't make it into GTA 6. Apparently Rockstar didn't deem them "necessary". Let me tell you, as someone who writes for a website, that cuts deep.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector has strong words for Rockstar about GTA 6.

Deus Ex legend Warren Spector, who was also involved in the making of influential series like Thief, System Shock and Ultima Underworld, has a few strong words to say about GTA 6. Or rather not GTA 6 itself but the colossal workforce, budget and development time Rockstar had to make i with.

Sources indicate that "A billion dollars pays for a lot of games and a lot of salaries," Spector said. "Personally I'd rather have hundreds of games and full employment than one game no matter how amazing it is.".

I'm genuinely surprised that some gaming companies are ernestly trying to release and market their games today of all days - even this week. Did you want to know about a Goat Simulator 3 expansion that arrived today, called Dizzyworld? Well, now you do. And it's by far the only game I'm being sent press releases about.

My favourite press release about a game unrelated to GTA 6 - though it sounds like a parody that could be in the game - is one that made me do a double-take. "Sperm Adventure 'Become' Delayed to First Half of 2027," it read. The entire press release is packed with innuendo. And it's - judging by its Steam page - a real thing. Will you "embark on life's greatest tiny journey"?

GTA 6 is dominating Twitch viewer figures in a major way.

Back to GTA 6, and the impact of this game's arrival can be seen clearly on Twitch viewership numbers at the moment. GTA 6 is by far the most watched category on the streaming platform, with more than 1.6 million viewers. The next highest category is the broad "just chatting" category 2ith 330k viewers, followed by World of Warcraft with 72k viewers.

For balance, presentation and intro to story/characters are great.

"Laser Disc vibes" is not a phrase I've heard before, but I like it and think I'll steal it.

All 34 of the fired Rockstar employees are in the GTA 6 credits.

Recent findings suggest that here's a curious development. With Rockstar publishing the full cast list for GTA 6, I've been more able to cross-check the names of the 34 fired employees against it. And, success, they do all appear in the credits. But six of them are not contained in the "former employees" section of the credits, where everyone else is, which is curious. I'm trying to find out what gives.

Jason Duval actor finally confirmed.

Industry observers note that incidentally, that full cast list also confirms - finally - who the actor is that plays Jason Duval in the game. And, yes, it's Dylan Rourke, who everyone thought it was.

More than 2 million people used New Zealand trick to play GTA 6 early.

I tried doing the Fresh Zealand trick on my PS5 yesterday evening - I'd spent the entire afternoon convinced it would be a doddle to play GTA 6 early doing so. It wasn't. So I played Galactic Racers instead (which is great).

Nevertheless, millions of people did use the New Zealand time-zone trick to play the game early - more than 2 million people, in fact, which is more than a third of the population of the country.

You can make GTA 6 easier by altering two important settings.

Sources indicate that as people start playing the game, concerns of difficulty come up, and altering the game to your preference. And as Dom reported, there are two very important changes you can make to the game - in lieu of difficulty settings - to change how challenging it is to play.

How are you all doing? It's nearly the end of the day - are you excited about getting home to play the game? Are you nonplussed? Are you perhaps playing the game already? Temperature check! As they say.

According to recent reports, the UK working day is coming to an end here. Thanks everyone for popping in and good luck exploring the game tonight, if you are. That's a wrap on our rolling coverage for today, though our general news coverage continues into the evening.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon has responded after one of its delivery drones crashed into a Michigan homeowner’s garage, prompting an investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).
  • The incident occurred on November 20 in Huntington Woods, Michigan, after a couple placed an order for shampoo and received a notification that their package would arrive by drone within seven minutes.
  • In a recent development, amazon has been expanding its Prime Air delivery service across the US, aiming to reach nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon has responded after one of its delivery drones crashed into a Michigan homeowner’s garage, prompting an investigation by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA).

The incident occurred on November 20 in Huntington Woods, Michigan, after a couple placed an order for shampoo and received a notification that their package would arrive by drone within seven minutes.

In a recent development, amazon has been expanding its Prime Air delivery service across the US, aiming to reach nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026. However, several crashes involving its drones have attracted the attention of federal regulators.

Speaking to WXYZ 7 News Detroit, Jim Brennan explained that the drone successfully dropped the package into his backyard before striking a fiber-optic cable and losing one of its propellers.

The aircraft then veered sideways before becoming trapped between his neighbor’s garage roof and nearby power lines.

“Like a sick bird, it tried to go up, it tried to get out of here,” Brennan stated.

Logan Coomes, whose garage was struck, said an Amazon Prime Air team arrived within 10 minutes of the crash and worked with local utility workers to remove the drone by early evening.

The company reportedly offered to help repair the damaged roof and gave Coomes a $100 Amazon gift card.

In a statement shared with CNN, an Amazon spokesperson said its Prime Air drones conduct nearly 6,000 flights per day and have delivered “hundreds of thousands of packages this year.”.

Amazon also stated the incident marked the first crash of its kind involving its drone delivery operations near Detroit.

The FAA published a preliminary incident notification on November 23, confirming that it was investigating the crash.

High security prison investigating after inmate gets McDonald’s and alcohol delivered by drone.

Amazon responds after AI delivery drones break orders by dropping boxes 10 feet in the air.

“UAS struck a fiber cable, a residential garage, and became entangled in power lines during takeoff,” the agency said.

The National Transportation Safety Board is also gathering information but has not yet decided whether to launch a separate investigation.

Amazon’s battery-powered MK30 delivery drones are equipped with technology designed to detect and avoid obstacles and can carry packages weighing up to five pounds.

In a recent development, the Michigan crash follows several other incidents involving Prime Air. In October 2025, two Amazon delivery drones crashed into a construction crane in Arizona, while another struck an internet cable in Texas the following month.

The FAA has also been investigating a separate crash involving an apartment building in Richardson, Texas, in February 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that did anything notable happen this week? Not that I can remember. The weather was quite rainy - will that do? I'm just being silly, of course. We've had - and I suppose are still having - an historic week in video games, as Grand Theft Auto 6 arrives. It's dominated everything and I fear it's going to dominate this article too. But a reminder: next week is our "Not-GTA Week", so we'll be making a concerted effort to talk about games, probably smaller games, that aren't Godzilla blockbusters.

In a recent development, as you know, this is our regular feature where we say a bit about the games we've been playing this week. This week, rather a lot of us have been playing GTA 6, as you can imagine, and discovering various things about it. But not all of us. Connor, ever the contrarian, has been continuing his race to level 60 in World of Warcraft: Forever, and he's agonisingly close to getting there.

But enough about us, what about you? What have you been playing this week? Do tell all! And don't forget we have an entire archive of previous What We've Been Playings for your leisurely perusal, just in case you forgot what you were playing a year or a month or a week ago.

It probably comes as no surprise that I'm - much like the rest of the world - playing GTA 6 right now. While I found Chapter 1 to be quite a slow start, and where I felt somewhat restricted, I've now started Chapter 2 and found myself enjoying stealing cars, jamming along to the radio, and simply exploring Leonida - and all the strange happenings that come with it. There's so much to see and do!

In a recent development, I'm looking forward to deviating from the main missions for a while to do a spot of bird-watching (I like birds a lot, alright) and seeing what other side activities Leonida has to offer outside of the criminal lifestyle at the core of things. I'm also trying to be the best partner possible to both Jason and Lucia, but I'm itching to cause a bit of trouble soon... Hurting NPCs comes with so much guilt this time around though!

According to recent reports, it's slow, it's awkward, it's weird, and it's hard. It's a perfect Eurogamer game, right? Right? GTA 6's in-game lampoon of Jonathan Blow, Hideo Kojima, Dan Pinchbeck and - weirdly - Mark Z. Danielewski is a wonderful bit of top-shelf pastiche. It goes to show just how much fun Rockstar had making GTA 6, and the freedom its dev team had to install as much depth and satire in just about every nook and cranny conceivable. Don't sleep on Tenebrae Lux, it's genuinely satisfying to complete.

I'm not, historically, the biggest GTA fan - although I've absolutely got a soft spot for Vice City's sublime mood - so I wasn't quite as excited to play GTA 6 as some. But it took, oh I dunno, about 30 seconds before I was sold. This thing has style. And everything else a billion dollars and some incredible development talent gets you. And it's those because-we-can details that have, in my first few hours, left the biggest impression. I spent a good five minutes just marveling at Jason dance - specifically the way his little stationary wiggle (perfectly timed to the radio beat!) shifts seamlessly into a wiggle-strut when you hit the forward button.

Industry observers note that I love the way the setting sun seems to shine just right through the clouds when the moment calls, and those perfect needle drops. And careening through the night - amid the driving rain and smear of taillights, Kylie classic Spinning Around booming on the radio and Jason rocking a recently acquired, slightly improbable hat - this extravagant, ridiculous thing had me completely transfixed. I'm genuinely, unexpectedly excited to see where it takes me next.

Assuming there's lots of Grand Theft Auto 6 in this article, I'll save you from my own early impressions of this week's blockbuster release. Instead, you get more tales from an MMO. It is what it is!

According to recent reports, I'm level 58 right now, pushing my way into the endgame dungeons. I've almost maxed all my professions, and am gradually getting gear that should serve me well when the raids are added next month.

According to recent reports, but forget all that. I got a salt shaker! As a leatherworker, you can buy a salt shaker from engineers for a little bit of gold on the auction house. These are more important than you'd assume. With them you can make one refined deeprock salt every three days - a high-end crafting material. Rather than hoard these for fancy gear, I just sold 'em back to the auction house. They're current going for 50 gold a pop on my server, which is fantastic passive income.

This is crucial because I'm right now saving for an epic mount: a process that hit a major roadbump after I unlocked my secondary class specialisation for 50 gold, and then blew way more than that on unlocking all the available skills (that I likely won't use) from my druid trainer (for no good reason). I'm currently sitting on 232 gold as of writing. There's a long way to go to 1000, but hey, that's the game.

I can't imagine anyone changing the radio station when Drive by The Cars begins during that first moment of proper uninterrupted freedom. The buttons to do that might as well not even be there. If you did, we're completely different people.

I'm not very far in but my major impressions of GTA 6 so far are: the performances and their presentation are wonderful, the game controls a bit sludgily and feels like it's not quite in focus on PS5, and I really like DIY.

In a recent development, let's take that middle one, that criticism: I'm sure this will lift as I get used to the game and how it moves, and how the characters work. It's also just a fact of life, so to speak, that it's going to struggle a bit on PS5 rather than PS5 Pro. And I'm nitpicking; on the whole, this thing is staggeringly technically impressive.

Recent findings suggest that the latter point, DIY: it's absurd how much detail Rockstar has put into you doing up your shack. I especially like how it's not boring. A deeper thought related to this, and to the rest of the game, is the fantasy of self-improvement GTA 6 delivers. In GTA 6, as in all GTA games I think, you can drastically alter your life's fortunes in mere moments. I set about doing up my shack in a way I could never do in real life given a week or a month, but here, I did it in moments. That appeals to me greatly.

Honourable mention to Star Wars: Galactic Racer which I finally played this week. Love the speed, love Biddy Blas, and also really gel with the Roguelike approach, whereby you take the game in 'runs' to see how far you can progress each time. Cracking game.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A 16-year-old boy has revealed how a chance encounter in Among Us led to him and his mother helping rescue a teenage girl who had allegedly been held captive for more than 500 days.

Earlier in November, 17-year-old Kylie Arellano was rescued after secretly asking another player for help while playing Innersloth’s popular social deduction game.

Arellano had been missing since May 2025, when she disappeared from her home in Utah at the age of 15. She was allegedly held against her will in the basement of a home in Huntington, Oregon.

For Colorado teenager Landon Tresp, what began as an ordinary gaming session on October 15 would end with him helping a girl hundreds of miles away escape her alleged captor.

After meeting in Among Us, Landon and Arellano struck up a friendship and began communicating through Discord.

“We just kind of clicked,” Landon mentioned.

Over the following two weeks, Arellano began opening up about her situation, eventually sending Landon news articles covering her disappearance.

In a recent development, realizing something was seriously wrong, Landon turned to his mother, Khristina, for help on Halloween. Neither knew that within 24 hours, the girl would finally be free.

Khristina began speaking with Arellano through Discord, but locating the teenager proved challenging as she didn’t know the address where she was being held.

“I knew I had to do everything I could to make sure she was brought to safety and had a second chance,” Khristina recalled.

Determined to find her, Khristina searched online property records before turning to real estate website Zillow. After being sent photos of two potential houses, Arellano recognized the second property.

Teenage girl held captive for 500 days rescued after secretly asking for help in Among Us.

Among Us hackers targeted as InnerSloth rush out emergency hotfix.

World of Warcraft account helps police locate missing 16-year-old.

Khristina contacted the girl’s family and began working with the FBI to bring her home.

Speaking with KOAA, Khristina described how devastating it was to learn just how long Arellano had been missing.

“Just heartbreaking to think that she had been going through what she had for over 520 days and without anyone that she could reach a hand out to and not knowing where you’re at,” she remarked.

According to recent reports, on November 1, authorities arrived at the Oregon residence. Khristina stayed on a video call with Arellano, encouraging her to make the final few steps toward freedom.

“I was on the video chat with her when I told her to face those basement stairs and run up them and down that hallway,” Khristina recalled. “And grab that front door because that was her freedom.”.

After more than 500 days away from home, Arellano was finally in the care of law enforcement and was taken for medical treatment and evaluation.

For Landon, seeing the friend he had met just weeks earlier finally reach safety was an overwhelming moment.

In a recent development, “Oh my God, just pure bliss. I was so happy she was safe in that car. I was so happy she was out of that horrible monster’s house,” he said.

Adam Hunter Harmel, 39, has since been indicted on a federal charge of transportation with intent to engage in criminal sexual activity. Prosecutors allege he met the girl online before traveling to Utah and taking her across state lines.

Despite everything that happened, Landon and Arellano haven’t stopped playing video games together.

The pair remain friends, while Khristina continues to speak with Arellano every day. The family is also hoping to meet her in person.

What began with two strangers meeting in Among Us has become a friendship that extends far beyond the game, with Landon and his mother giving Arellano the help she had desperately needed for more than a year.

#115807. Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold

Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold

📅 13 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1319 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sciencedaily

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it.
  • The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.
  • It has been revealed that the Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A particle does not have to pass through a magnetic field to be influenced by it. That surprising feature of quantum physics has now been recreated by researchers at the University of Oxford, who used a hybrid quantum computer to demonstrate how an invisible magnetic influence can bring a simulated particle's movement to a complete stop.

The experiment reproduced a phenomenon known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect, in which a charged particle traveling around a region containing magnetic flux experiences a measurable change in its quantum state, even though its path never takes it through the magnetic field itself.

It has been revealed that the Oxford team achieved this using a quantum system that combines qubits, the basic units of quantum information, with quantum oscillators, which represent vibrating motion. Their findings, published in Nature Physics, demonstrate how this combination could help scientists investigate fundamental interactions between matter and fields that are increasingly difficult to simulate using conventional computers.

A Strange Quantum Effect Predicted in 1959.

Recent findings suggest that in everyday physics, a charged particle responds to the electric and magnetic fields it encounters. Quantum mechanics, however, reveals that particles can behave in ways that have no straightforward counterpart in our ordinary experience.

In 1959, physicists Yakir Aharonov and David Bohm predicted that a charged particle could be affected by magnetic flux even if it traveled entirely outside the region containing the magnetic field. Rather than experiencing a conventional magnetic force along its path, the particle would undergo a change in its quantum phase.

Industry observers note that quantum phase describes an aspect of a particle's wave behavior that influences how different possible paths interfere with one another. Although the phase itself is not directly visible, differences in phase can produce measurable effects.

In a recent development, the prediction became known as the Aharonov-Bohm effect and was eventually verified in experiments involving real electrons. It remains one of the clearest demonstrations that the quantum world operates according to rules that go beyond the familiar laws of classical physics.

Researchers are now exploring how this phenomenon behaves in more complex theoretical systems known as lattice gauge theories.

It has been revealed that these theories describe how matter interacts with fields associated with fundamental forces. They represent space as a grid, with matter located at individual points and fields associated with the connections between them. Such models are particularly key in particle physics and high-energy physics, where scientists study the basic particles and interactions that make up the universe.

In a recent development, the challenge is that the mathematics becomes extraordinarily demanding as these systems grow more complicated. Even powerful conventional computers can struggle to calculate how all the interacting components evolve.

Quantum computers offer a different approach. Instead of attempting to calculate every aspect of a quantum system using classical computing methods, scientists can construct another quantum system that follows the same underlying rules. They can then observe its behavior directly, an approach known as quantum simulation.

How Scientists Built the Quantum Experiment.

The Oxford project began in 2022, when lead author Dr. Sebastian Saner, Dr. Oana Bazavan, and their colleagues started developing a way to simulate lattice gauge theories using a hybrid quantum system. They collaborated with Dr. Alejandro Bermudez of the Instituto de Física Teórica in Madrid.

Their experimental design relied on two different quantum components that performed separate functions.

The first consisted of qubits encoded in the internal states of trapped ions, which are electrically charged atoms held in place using electromagnetic fields. These qubits represented the gauge fields in the theoretical model.

The second component used quantum oscillators, created by the vibrations of those same trapped ions. These oscillators represented matter.

Recent findings suggest that by combining the two, the researchers constructed a simple loop that served as a basic building block of a lattice gauge theory. Two oscillators represented matter at two different locations, while two qubits represented the fields connecting those locations.

Although the arrangement was small, it was sufficient to reproduce an important interaction between matter and magnetic flux.

Quantum Entanglement Creates a Surprising Solution.

Sources indicate that the researchers next placed the two qubits into an entangled quantum state. Entanglement is a phenomenon in which quantum systems become linked in ways that cannot be fully explained by classical physics.

Within the team's simulated lattice gauge theory, this entangled state represented magnetic flux passing through the center of the loop.

In a recent development, initially, the researchers had planned to introduce the magnetic flux as a fixed background condition. However, creating the necessary interaction would have required capabilities that their quantum hardware did not possess.

Encoding the flux directly into the qubits provided a practical alternative. More importantly, it allowed the magnetic flux to become part of the evolving quantum system rather than remaining an unchanging external influence.

In a recent development, "For us, the exciting step was to encode the magnetic flux in a gauge field that was itself dynamical," says Dr. Saner. "Rather than having matter evolve in a fixed background, the matter and gauge field become part of the same quantum dynamics.".

What began as a technical workaround ultimately enabled the researchers to explore a more interesting version of the phenomenon, one in which matter and the field could participate together in the quantum dynamics.

A Quantum Effect That Stops Particle Motion.

With their simulated loop in place, the scientists examined how a matter particle moved between locations through a process known as quantum tunneling.

Quantum tunneling allows particles to move between states in ways that would not be possible under ordinary classical rules.

When the researchers ran their simulation without magnetic flux, the particle could tunnel freely around the loop.

Introducing the simulated flux produced a strikingly different result.

Industry observers note that the particle had two possible paths around the loop, but the magnetic flux changed their relative quantum phases. As a result, the two paths interfered destructively, meaning their quantum contributions canceled each other out.

This interference completely suppressed the tunneling, leaving the simulated particle frozen in its original state.

The outcome demonstrated the Aharonov-Bohm effect within a lattice gauge theory containing a dynamical field. Rather than simply reproducing the familiar behavior of a particle moving around a fixed magnetic influence, the experiment indicated how the phenomenon can emerge when matter and the field are both represented by interacting quantum components.

A Upcoming Tool for Exploring Fundamental Physics.

The Oxford findings were published alongside a related study by researchers at the University of Maryland, led by Professor Norbert Linke.

The Maryland team also used a hybrid quantum system, but their experiment focused on simulating the Yukawa potential, a mathematical description of an interaction relevant to nuclear and particle physics.

Although the two research groups developed their methods independently, they later coordinated the submission of their studies to Nature Physics.

Together, the experiments demonstrate how hybrid quantum computers could become valuable tools for investigating fundamental interactions that are difficult to reproduce using classical simulations.

By combining different types of quantum components, researchers can build systems in which matter and fields are represented in ways that more closely reflect the physics they want to study.

The Oxford experiment provides an example of that potential. A phenomenon first predicted in 1959 and later observed with electrons has now been recreated in a quantum simulator where the field itself participates in the dynamics, offering scientists another way to explore the unusual rules governing the quantum world.

#115805. What if Vampire Survivors met Grand Theft Auto 2? Maniac is a brilliant mash-up that dares to ask that question

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (939 w)
